blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
To import is to bring goods from another country. To export is to send goods to another country. These two words are very common in business.

Czarnikow exports sugar from Brazil to India, Europe and Africa. The sugar leaves a port in Brazil. Then it travels by ship to another country.

Today we learn five words: import, export, country, port and shipment. We also use there is and there are to talk about ports, ships and buyers.

items.q: What does "to import" mean?
options: To bring goods from another country
To send goods to another country
items.why: "To import is to bring goods from another country."

items.q: Where does Czarnikow export sugar?
items.why: "Czarnikow exports sugar from Brazil to India, Europe and Africa."

items.q: How does the sugar travel to another country?
items.why: "Then it travels by ship to another country."

items.q: The text suggests that Brazil is…
items.why: Inferência: a Czarnikow exporta açúcar do Brasil, então o Brasil vende (exporta) açúcar.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: import and export are not useful in business
import and export are common business words
there are no ports in Brazil
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que essas duas palavras são muito comuns em negócios.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Ethan no porto. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hello, my name is Ethan. Welcome to the port of Santos, here in Brazil. Let me show you a simple flow.

Look. There is a big ship at the port today. There are many containers of sugar on the ship. The sugar is from Brazil. This is an export.

The ship leaves Santos. It travels for many days. Then it arrives at a port in India. In India, this same sugar is an import. So one shipment is an export for us and an import for them.

There is one shipment on the water now. There are three buyers in India who wait for it. There is no problem with the cargo. Everything is ready.

Remember: export is to send, import is to bring. Same sugar, two words. It only depends on the country. There is always a next step.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Where is Ethan?
options: At the port of Santos in Brazil
items.why: "Welcome to the port of Santos, here in Brazil."

items.q: What is on the ship?
items.why: "There are many containers of sugar on the ship."

items.q: When the sugar arrives in India, it is…
items.why: "Then it arrives at a port in India. In India, this same sugar is an import."

items.q: Ethan suggests that export and import…
options: describe the same shipment from two countries
items.why: Inferência: "Same sugar, two words. It only depends on the country."

items.q: How would you describe the situation with the cargo?
options: It is late and full of problems
items.why: Inferência: "There is no problem with the cargo. Everything is ready."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Brazil is a big country." A country is…
options: a nation, like Brazil or India
items.why: Country = país, uma nação como o Brasil ou a Índia.

items.q: "The ship is at the port." A port is…
options: a place where ships arrive and leave
items.why: Port = porto, lugar onde os navios chegam e partem.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "There is one big ___ of sugar on the ship."
items.why: Shipment = carregamento/remessa, o que vai no navio.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We ___ sugar from Brazil to other countries."
items.why: Export = exportar: enviar mercadorias para outro país.

items.q: "India needs to import sugar." To import means to…
items.why: Import = importar: trazer mercadorias de outro país.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples de negócios sobre porto e mercadorias. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We ship out the sugar tomorrow." To ship out means to…
options: send goods away, usually by ship
items.why: Ship out = despachar/enviar a mercadoria.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the shipment." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new plan next month." To roll out means to…
options: start using it, step by step
items.why: Roll out = colocar em prática aos poucos.

items.q: "Please follow up with the buyer in India." To follow up means to…
options: talk again later to check on something
items.why: Follow up = dar continuidade, entrar em contato de novo para acompanhar.

items.q: "The sugar is popular, so we always sell out fast." To sell out means to…
items.why: Sell out = vender tudo, esgotar o estoque.
